summary: Intermittent duplicate tool invocations when client backpressure semaphore triggers retries during streaming
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent duplicate external tool invocations (webhook POSTs) when using streaming responses with client-side backpressure semaphores.
Impact: Duplicate downstream side-effects (order creation) observed ~0.1-0.5% of streaming sessions during high throughput. Customer on Dedicated tier; business impact moderate (order duplicates require manual reconciliation).
Environment: BrightCart production, dedicated pool in us-east-1, SDKs in Python v1.8.0 and TypeScript v1.7.9, edge sidecar (third-party) sits in front of SDK client.
Steps to reproduce:
  1) Start a streaming chat session that triggers multiple tool calls (3-5) in a single conversation turn.
  2) Client uses a semaphore limited to 2 concurrent outbound tool confirmations to avoid overload.
  3) Under sustained load, the semaphore blocks confirm ACKs and SDK initiates retry logic for pending funcalls after ack_timeout.
  4) Downstream webhook receives duplicate POSTs for same logical tool invocation (same payload) in ~1/1000 requests.
Logs / Evidence: Customer provided sample correlation IDs and webhook payloads (attached in ticket), SDK debug logs show: "funcall: sent", "ack: delayed by semaphore", "client retry: triggered", and server shows two distinct inbound deliveries with identical nonce.
Customer expectation: At-most-once side-effect for tool invocations or clear guidance on recommended patterns when using client-side backpressure.
Requested: Guidance on SDK config and platform mitigations; ask whether Redwood runtime should suppress repeated deliveries in this scenario.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Priya): Acknowledged, asked for SDK debug logs, sample webhook receipts, and whether BrightCart uses any proxy that could buffer traffic. Requested safe mode steps (increase semaphore, set ack_timeout=60s) to test.

2026-03-10 - Customer (BrightCart SRE, Maria Chen): Uploaded webhook timestamps and SDK logs. Confirmed they run an edge sidecar (CloudFlare Worker) that may chunk responses. Performed quick test increasing semaphore to 4 and saw duplicate rate drop but not eliminated.

2026-03-11 - Support (Liam): Reproduced locally by running Python SDK streaming harness with artificial delayed ACK behavior. Observed race between client retry timer and resumed ACK path that resulted in duplicate funcall deliveries. Hypothesis: client retry triggers full re-send while server treats delayed in-flight confirmation as separate delivery due to nonce being omitted when edge sidecar rewrites headers.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Checked serving-runtime logs for customer pool; server emitted single funcall event, but webhook gateway shows two deliveries. Edge-proxy logs show it split/rewrote X-Idempotency header on HTTP/2 chunk boundary. Opened internal investigation to confirm header propagation across edge proxies. Linked INT-22110 for infra tracking.
2026-03-12 - Support (Liam): Sent temporary mitigation steps to customer and provided SDK patch recommendations. Customer to validate in staging.
2026-03-12 - Customer (Maria Chen): Applying recommended SDK settings to staging and will run load test overnight; requested ETA for platform-side fix or compatibility guidance.
investigation_notes: Reproduction summary: Local harness using SDK v1.8.0 with simulated ACK delay reproduces duplicate webhook POST when HTTP/2 header frames split idempotency header.

Hypothesis: Edge proxy or sidecar is splitting or normalizing idempotency header (X-Per-Message-Nonce) during streaming chunking; SDK retry logic resends full funcall without matching nonce in upstream view, causing duplicate execution.
Observed that increasing client semaphore reduces duplicates but does not eliminate; indicates timing/race rather than pure concurrency bug.
Serving runtime appears to emit a single funcall event; duplicate deliveries originate at gateway/edge layer based on rewritten header values.
Related internal issue: INT-22110 (edge-proxy header rewrite during chunked streaming) may be root cause.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds provided to customer (validated by BrightCart in staging):
  1) Upgrade SDKs to Python v1.8.2 / TS v1.8.1 which include client-side change: always attach explicit per-message nonce in message body when streaming to tolerate header rewrite.
  2) Increase ack_timeout to 45s and temporarily raise semaphore limit to 4 to reduce race frequency while testing.
  3) Configure edge sidecar to preserve X-Per-Message-Nonce header or disable streaming chunking rewrite where possible.

Platform mitigation: SRE/infrastructure to deploy guard in gateway to canonicalize idempotency nonce from message body into upstream header when missing. INT-22110 assigned to infra; target rollout 2026-03-18.
Long-term: Add end-to-end test for header preservation across HTTP/2/edge chunking in CI and enhance SDK to embed canonical nonce in both header and payload.
Customer outcome: BrightCart accepted temporary workaround and will schedule SDK upgrade next maintenance window. They requested follow-up when INT-22110 fixed.
